lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Denise Gadelha Rocha | Lesson 9 -- Executive Email and Written Authority

listenings.text: I get somewhere between two and three hundred messages a day, and I want to be honest with you about what I actually read. The subject line and the first two lines. That is the whole decision. Everything after that gets read only if those two lines have earned it. So the subject line has to carry the ask and the date, not the topic. Colombia update tells me nothing and it will sit there for a week. Colombia renewal, decision needed by Thursday tells me what you want and when, and I can act on it between two meetings. If I cannot see the ask straight away, the message goes into the pile I will get to on Sunday, and Sunday is where good work goes to die. One more rule, and people always resist it. If you have three things to ask me, send three emails with one ask in each. You will get three answers. Send one email with three asks and you will get an answer to the first one.

For a long time I opened every English email with two or three lines of warmth, the way I would in my own language. I hope this message finds you well. Apologies for the extra work. Thank you so much in advance. I stopped, and not because anybody was rude about it. I stopped because I finally understood how those lines were landing. They were reading as hesitation, and hesitation from a director reads as doubt about her own request. Here is what took me years to accept. Directness does not sound childish. The pile of apologies around the ask is what sounds childish. So the warm sentence still exists in my emails, but it lives at the end now, and it is one sentence instead of a paragraph. And I never apologise for a deadline. A deadline is a fact of the business, not a favour I am asking for. I state it, and I say what happens if it moves.

extra_audio.text: By Thursday we will have closed the Colombian renewal, and I need your sign-off on the wording before then. The thread below has the two clauses that changed, and the rest is the boilerplate we have used since March. I have looped in Mexico, because the same wording will be going to them in April. If I have not heard from you by Wednesday evening, I will chase once and then proceed as drafted.
